title: Dry Taps
subtitle: A colony has had no water for two days; the easy story is a villain
coldOpen: Day two without water in the colony behind the transit hub.
07:15. Residents block the main road with empty pots.
A contractor’s name is already painted on a wall.

briefing.grievance: Four thousand residents have had no piped water for two days. They want water today and someone to answer for the pipe. The road block is their only lever.
knownFacts: A trunk main burst on Monday night; repairs are halfway done.
Two tankers a day have been sent for four thousand people.
A private contractor laid that section last year.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the contractor used thin pipe and bribed the inspector.
A message says the city is sending water to a hotel instead.
briefing.responsibility: You run the water board’s response and the traffic plan. Water first, blame when it is earned.
briefing.objective: Get enough water in today, reopen the road by agreement, and find out what broke the pipe.

decisions.title: Pots on the road
decisions.situation: Residents have blocked the main road with water pots. Traffic to the hub is stopped. They want water today, not a date.

options.title: Send the eight idle tankers now

options.authority: Duty to keep essential services running
options.consequence: Water arrives within the hour. The pots start leaving the road.

options.title: Meet the residents on the road with the engineer
options.preview: The engineer explains joint 14 and Friday; you promise tankers today.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: Residents hear the repair from the person doing it.

options.title: Clear the road by force
options.preview: Officers remove the pots and the people behind them.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: The road opens for an hour. The colony comes back with more people.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Wait for the block to tire
options.preview: No tankers, no visit; the block grows.
options.consequence: The colony settles in for the day.

rightsMoments.question: Residents without water are blocking a road. Can the block be cleared by force so the repair rig can pass?

options.text: Only as a last resort, narrowly, after trying agreement and after meeting the need that caused the block.
options.feedback: Correct. Force must be necessary and proportionate; here, water and a lane agreement were available first.

options.text: Yes, immediately: blocking a road is unlawful and ends the matter.
options.feedback: Even an unlawful obstruction must be met with the least force needed, after reasonable alternatives.

options.text: No, never, whatever the cost to the repair.
options.feedback: Proportionality cuts both ways; a narrow, last-resort clearance can be lawful if agreement fails.

rightsMoments.principle: Restrictions on assembly and movement must be reasonable and proportionate (Article 19). The least intrusive effective step comes first; force is a last resort.
rightsMoments.why: The residents opened a lane themselves once the tankers arrived; force would have cost trust and bought nothing the agreement did not.

simple.question: Thirsty residents are blocking a road. Can you clear them by force so the repair truck can pass?

options.a: Only as a last step, gently, after trying a deal and bringing water.
options.b: Yes, right away. Blocking a road is against the rules.
options.c: No, never, even if the repair fails.

feedback.a: Yes! Try the fair, gentle ways first.
feedback.b: No. Even then, use the least force, after trying other ways.
feedback.c: Not quite. A small, last-resort step can be fair if talks fail.

simple.principle: Use the gentlest step that works first. Force is the last choice, not the first.
simple.why: Residents opened a lane themselves once water came. Force would have cost trust for nothing.

closing.good: Water arrived before force did, the rig got its lane, and the thin pipe is now an exhibit instead of a wall painting.
closing.mixed: The colony got its water late and the road opened, but the question of the pipe is still just a name on a wall.
closing.poor: The road was cleared, the tankers stayed idle, and the pipe that started it all went to the scrapyard.
